title: TKT Module 1 · Additional Practice Test (20 questions)
source: Teacher-created practice based on the supplied Cambridge TKT sample papers

questions.text: In “They have lived here for five years”, what is the main use of the present perfect?
options: To describe a situation that began in the past and continues now
To describe a repeated future arrangement
To describe a finished action at a definite past time

questions.text: Which word is a preposition in “The keys are under the newspaper”?
Which word contains a negative prefix?
Which is a compound noun?
Which pair is a common verb + noun collocation?
In “She speaks remarkably clearly”, what does “remarkably” modify?
Which sentence contains a defining relative clause?
options: My brother, who lives in Leeds, is a nurse.
It was raining, which surprised us.
The book that you lent me is excellent.

questions.text: Which word is the object pronoun?
Which sentence uses “will” to make a prediction based on an opinion?
options: I think the team will win tonight.
She is meeting the manager at six.
Look at those clouds; it is going to rain.

questions.text: Which is a minimal pair?
What is the usual word stress in “photography”?
Which is a voiced consonant sound?
Which sentence is a first conditional?
options: If I had more time, I would travel.
If it rains, we will stay inside.
If she had studied, she would have passed.

questions.text: What is the function of “Would you mind closing the window?”
Which is an example of a lexical set?
A learner says “I goed to the market.” Which error is this?
Which is a receptive skill?
What does “bilingual” mean?
options: learning a language for the first time

questions.text: Which word is a demonstrative pronoun in “Those are mine”?
In “Could you give me a hand?”, what does the phrase mean?

title: TKT Module 2 · Additional Practice Test (20 questions)
source: Teacher-created practice based on the supplied Cambridge TKT sample papers

questions.text: A teacher asks learners to read a short article quickly and choose its best title. What is the main reading subskill?
Learners listen to a train announcement to write down the platform number. What is the main subskill?
At the start of a lesson, learners brainstorm words connected with “holidays”. What is the main aim?
Learners compare two pictures and find ten differences. Which speaking skill is practised most?
Which activity focuses on accurate letter formation?
options: writing a review for a website

questions.text: A lesson plan says learners will “understand the past simple”. What would make this aim more useful?
options: Learners will use regular past forms to describe a finished weekend.

questions.text: What is the main purpose of a warmer?
options: to introduce a brief engaging start and focus learners

questions.text: Learners predict an article’s content from its headline and photograph. What are they using?
Which resource is most suitable for showing how a word is pronounced?
Why might a teacher use realia in a lesson on food?
Learners choose the correct verb form from options in a sentence. What kind of practice is this?
Learners role-play ordering food using their own ideas. What kind of practice is this?
Which is a suitable lesson aim for practising skimming?
options: Learners will copy every sentence accurately.
Learners will identify the main idea of a text quickly.

questions.text: Why include an answer key with a self-study worksheet?
options: so learners do not need to read instructions
so learners can check their own work
so the worksheet has more questions

questions.text: Learners put mixed-up sentences into a logical order. What are they focusing on?
A teacher elicits examples before explaining a grammar rule. What approach is this?
Which is the best way to check instructions before a pair task?
options: ask a learner to explain what they will do

questions.text: A teacher plans a backup activity in case a task finishes early. This is an example of:
Learners listen to a dialogue and complete missing words. What is the main focus?
Which activity best practises proofreading?
options: learners find and correct errors in a draft
learners listen for the main idea

title: TKT Module 3 · Additional Practice Test (20 questions)
source: Teacher-created practice based on the supplied Cambridge TKT sample papers

questions.text: A teacher says “A pharmacy is a shop where you buy medicine.” What is the teacher doing?
A teacher asks “What did the character do after she missed the bus?” What is the main purpose?
options: checking understanding of a specific detail

questions.text: A learner says “He go yesterday.” The teacher replies “He … yesterday?” What technique is used?
Which instruction is clearest for a pair speaking task?
options: Discuss the questions with your partner for three minutes.
You know, perhaps do something with these questions.

questions.text: A teacher asks learners to skim a text and say what it is mainly about. This is reading for:
Why might a teacher nominate a learner after asking a question to the whole class?
options: to check spelling in a text
to give every learner more planning time
to invite a particular learner to respond

questions.text: While pairs do a fluency activity, the teacher notes recurring errors and does not interrupt. What is the teacher doing?
Which feedback is most formative?
options: Your examples are clear; add a past-time phrase to make the order clearer.

questions.text: A teacher claps twice to regain attention. This is mainly a way of:
Learners work in pairs, each with different information needed to complete a schedule. What is this?
Which teacher action best supports learner autonomy?
options: translating every new word for them
showing learners how to use a dictionary independently

questions.text: A teacher says “First read alone. Then compare answers with a partner.” Why is this order useful?
options: it makes the task sequence clear

questions.text: One learner answers every question. What could the teacher do to distribute participation?
options: use pair discussion before nominating different learners

questions.text: Which is an example of delayed error correction?
options: giving the answer before learners speak
interrupting every sentence to correct it
writing selected errors on the board after a fluency task

questions.text: A teacher demonstrates a dialogue with one learner before asking pairs to practise. The teacher is:
Learners choose which of three solutions to a problem is best and explain why. This mainly practises:
A teacher asks “Can you give me an example?” after a learner gives a general answer. The teacher is:
What is the main benefit of using pair work?
options: it removes the need for instructions
it guarantees every answer is correct

questions.text: A learner cannot remember a word. The teacher says “It is a place where you borrow books.” This is:
At the end of a lesson, learners write one thing they learned and one question they still have. This is useful for:

title: TKT Module 3 · M3 V62 Source Test (20 questions)
source: User-supplied M3 V62 PDF; questions adapted into interactive multiple-choice format and answers solved from the classroom-teaching context

questions.text: A teacher says, “That’s right, he’s wearing a jacket. Are jackets normally long or short?” Which classroom function is illustrated?
A teacher says, “Then the three friends woke up and continued their journey.” What is the teacher doing?
A teacher says, “OK, you like that picture. Can you tell your partner why you like it?” What is the main function?
A teacher says, “Can everyone stop writing now? Pass your paper to the person on your left.” This is an example of:
A teacher explains that “a quarter past three” is the same as “three fifteen”. Which function is this?
Before reading a text, a teacher asks learners to suggest clothes normally worn only in cold weather. What is the teacher doing?
Learners have completed a pre-reading task and made predictions. Which instruction best checks those predictions during reading?
options: Read carefully and tell me the gist.
Look at the text and check whether your ideas were correct.
Read quickly and choose the best title.

questions.text: A teacher wants elementary learners to become interested in a topic using a picture. Which task best invites them to speculate?
options: Tell me where the picture is.
Answer three factual questions with a partner.
Say what you think the people have been doing.

questions.text: A learner asks whether she can express a sentence in a different way. Which response is least appropriate for a pre-intermediate learner?
options: You can, but it sounds too formal.
If you say it like that, it will not be very clear what you mean.
It’s highly unlikely you would hear anyone express it in that way.

questions.text: A teacher wants to find out whether learners remember the meaning of “safe”. Which question most directly checks recall?
options: Can anyone give a word which is the opposite of safe?
Where did we see safe yesterday?
I think you have all seen safe before. Do you understand it?

questions.text: Learners are writing a complaint to a bank manager. What is the best advice for their first draft?
options: Concentrate on communicating the complaint; refine form later.
Register does not matter at any stage.
Only check paragraph links before writing any content.

questions.text: A learner struggles to pronounce “atmosphere”. Which teacher action gives useful pronunciation support?
options: Show the spelling and have learners identify the main stress after listening.
Say the spelling is difficult, so they should guess how to write it.
Tell them the letters ph are always pronounced /p/.

questions.text: Before a listening interview, a teacher asks questions about the topic to focus learners. Which activity is this?
Before a speaking task, learners share as many ideas as possible about the topic. What is this?
A teacher watches pair work to check that learners are following the task instructions. The teacher is:
In an essay, a learner writes “the huge park in centre”. Which area needs correction?
In the same essay, a learner writes “its nice that ice-cream is available”. Which error is illustrated?
In group planning, one learner says, “Are we supposed to be talking about our home town or the town we’re studying in?” What is the speaker doing?
During a fluency role-play, a teacher notes recurring errors and discusses them after the activity. This is:
A teacher uses a correction code on learners’ essays. What does this technique mainly encourage?
options: Learners to identify and correct their own errors
The teacher to rewrite every essay
